title: Palindrome Partitioning
prompt:
Split the string `s` into pieces so that every piece is a palindrome. Return all possible ways to do this, in any order.

**Example**: `"aab"` → `[["a","a","b"],["aa","b"]]`.

**Constraints**: 1 ≤ s.length ≤ 16, lowercase letters.
hints: The first piece of any valid split is some palindromic prefix of `s`. Once you pick it, what problem is left?
Backtrack on a `start` index: try each `end` so that `s.substring(start, end)` is a palindrome, add it to the path, and recurse from `end`. When `start == s.length()`, record a copy.
Check palindromes with two pointers moving inward. Skip any prefix that isn't a palindrome, and remove the piece after recursing.

solution.explanation: Each level commits to one palindromic piece and leaves the rest of the string to deeper calls, so every root-to-leaf path in the recursion is one valid split. Skipping prefixes that aren't palindromes prunes early. O(n·2ⁿ) time worst case (for example, all the same letter), O(n) recursion depth.
